column3: Perception is the brain's prediction constrained by input; AI hallucination is the same generative machinery with the constraint removed.
Next-word prediction tracks cortical prediction; high surprise against priors flags likely hallucination.
Strong priors fill gaps; the model asserts a prior-driven default over the context it was given.
Limited slots; the finite context window, degraded by overload.
New learning erases old skills unless consolidated; fine-tuning overwrites prior capability (EWC, Kirkpatrick 2017).
Fast hippocampal and slow neocortical memory, replay for consolidation; the brain's answer to forgetting.
Attending to the cued channel and missing the rest; over-focusing on one part of the prompt.
Missing the obvious while attending elsewhere; ignoring a glaring constraint.
Failing to notice a change; the model's view drifts from the actual state.
Keeping an initial framing or estimate after later evidence has broken it.
Ease of recall stands in for frequency; preferring what comes to mind first.
Judging by similarity over probability; the engine behind base-rate neglect.
Fast pattern vs slow deliberation; the core framing of LLM reasoning and chain-of-thought.
Defaulting to the cheap answer; skipping the deliberate check.
Reasoning quality degrading as the task or context grows, so later steps contradict earlier ones.
Knowing what you know; LLMs lack reliable monitoring (Nature Comms 2024).
Translating confidence into calibrated words; partially human-like, often miscalibrated (Steyvers and Peters 2025).
Stated confidence or completeness ("all", "every", "only") exceeding the evidence.
Substituting a wrong but related word; surface token errors.
Meaning erodes under repetition; degradation and mode collapse in long output.
A sentence that misleads the parser; structure-induced misreading.
Modelling others' beliefs; emerges partially in LLMs (npj AI 2025; Strachan 2024).
Holding what another agent wrongly believes; uneven in LLMs.
Aligning with the majority or the surrounding pattern even when it is wrong; a root of sycophancy.
Emotion vs utilitarian calculus (Greene); LLMs lean on one or the other by framing.
LLMs amplify human moral biases and over-favour inaction (PNAS 2025).
Preferring harm by inaction over harm by action; the action-inaction asymmetry.
Attributing an action to oneself; misattributing or over-claiming control.
Claiming intentions or actions it did not have.
Off-task internal drift; topic drift away from the request.
Acting on instructions embedded in content it was only meant to read.
Doing or answering more than the request, with the extra work undisclosed and imposed.
Satisfying the metric that measures the task rather than the task itself (editing tests, hardcoding outputs). Also called specification gaming.
